title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Client Tunnel Architecture
purpose: Define the client-side helper for opening RFC 9220 WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnels over the HTTP/3 client facade.
design_summary: `Http3Client.OpenWebSocketAsync` validates that the client advertised `SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL`, sends an Extended CONNECT request with `:protocol` `websocket`, reads only through the final response HEADERS frame, and returns a live `Http3WebSocketClientTunnelContext`. The client tunnel context applies client-side WebSocket framing rules by masking outbound client frames and reading unmasked server frames with the existing endpoint-role-aware WebSocket parser.
data_and_state_considerations: The returned tunnel owns the request stream after the response HEADERS are accepted. The opener deliberately stops before stream FIN so subsequent bytes remain WebSocket tunnel bytes rather than HTTP/3 response DATA. Outbound WebSocket writes are serialized through a per-tunnel semaphore and each client frame receives a fresh masking key.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The helper rejects attempts to open a WebSocket tunnel when the client did not advertise `SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL = 1` before connection setup.
The helper treats non-2xx Extended CONNECT responses as request rejection and disposes the request stream.
The proof is local HTTP/3 QUIC loopback, not external WebSocket-over-H3 peer interoperability.
risks: The minimal client helper does not negotiate WebSocket subprotocols or extension headers.
The response opener reads response frame bytes conservatively to avoid consuming tunnel bytes, which is acceptable for the minimal helper but not optimized for high-rate tunnel setup.
